newsitem.title: USA: AT&T new initiatives cut Q1 earnings by $0.25.
newsitem.headline: AT&T new initiatives cut Q1 earnings by $0.25.

text.p: AT&T Corp on Monday said that investment to be ready for new competition and new markets cut its earnings by $0.25 per share in the first quarter of 1997. It cut year ago earnings by $0.10.

Earnings per share came in at $0.69, 25 percent below the year ago figure of $0.92 and in line with the prediction given by the firm at an analysts' meeting in March, as well as matching analysts' consensus estimates on First Call.
Analysts were in March told that earnings per share for the first quarter would be about 10 percent below the $0.76 per share earned in the fourth quarter of 1996.

Long distance calling volumes rose 6.7 percent from a year ago, but revenues from those services rose only 0.6 percent to $11.51 billion. Volumes from consumer long distance were flat, while revenues fell one percent to $6.057 billion, AT&T said.
Analysts focus on the gap between revenue and volume as an indicator of pricing and retention of high value customers.
AT&T said the gap between the two in the consumer area was large was because of the use of free minutes on the network as a marketing and customer-retention tool.
Business long distance revenues rose 2.4 percent compared with a year ago on a double-digit volume rise.

The gap between volume and revenue growth was driven by lower margins on new business contracts because of increased competition and an increased volume of low-price government traffic relating to an Internal Revenue Service contract.

Wireless service revenues rose 13.9 percent to $1.02 billion from $896 million a year ago. Subscribers jumped 25.8 percent to 5.32 million. It said growth rates were cut by the sale of some cellular properties in the 1996 fourth quarter.
Total capital spending for the quarter was $1 billion, up from $800 million a year ago, mostly because of investment in new initiatives and building up the long distance network.
The overall financial effect was lower, however because of the cash infusion from disposals, bringing net capital spending down to $600 million from $700 million a year ago.

Financial services revenues plunged 18.7 percent in the first quarter a year ago because of the accounting treatment of the $3 billion securitization program for AT&T Universal Card receivables in 1996.
However, operating income at the unit rose to $52 million from $50 million a year ago, helped by a 21 percent fall in operating costs helped by the securitizatipn program.

AT&T said it was now offering total local calling resale services in four states -- California, Connecticut, Illinois and Michigan -- and was offering business local services through AT&T Digital Link services in 45 states.

Maureen Tart, AT&T vice president and controller, told a conference call that local service telemarketing calls were winning 25 percent of the customers contacted in the four total resale states, up from 20 percent initially.
Local, one of the projects contributing to the $0.25 per share cost of new initiatives, reduced earnings by $200 million or $0.08 per share.
No breakout was given for the cost of the other initiatives which include Worldnet Internet services, digital wireless expansion, the expansion of data services and international ventures.
